details: picklescan before 0.0.22 only considers standard pickle file extensions in the scope for its vulnerability scan. An attacker could craft a malicious model that uses Pickle and include a malicious pickle file with a non-standard file extension. Because the malicious pickle file inclusion is not considered as part of the scope of picklescan, the file would pass security checks and appear to be safe, when it could instead prove to be problematic.

A vulnerability in the GraphCypherQAChain class of langchain-ai/langchain-community version 0.2.5 allows for SQL injection through prompt injection. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data manipulation, data exfiltration, denial of service (DoS) by deleting all data, breaches in multi-tenant security environments, and data integrity issues. Attackers can create, update, or delete nodes and relationships without proper authorization, extract sensitive data, disrupt services, access data across different tenants, and compromise the integrity of the database.

notes.text: The Go standard library function net/url.Parse insufficiently validated the host/authority component and accepted some invalid URLs by effectively treating garbage before an IP-literal as ignorable. The function should have rejected this as invalid.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: Incorrect parsing of IPv6 host literals in net/url
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat evaluates this vulnerability as having an Important severity because unauthenticated remote attackers can target exposed Go services over the network to trigger severe denial-of-service conditions or validation discrepancies without requiring elevated privileges. Across standard Red Hat environments—including OpenShift Container Platform and Red Hat Enterprise Linux container tools—many components rely on the core Go runtime to process user-supplied addresses and endpoints. Although improper handling of malformed host segments in web addresses can disrupt network-facing daemons, the vulnerability cannot be leveraged for arbitrary code execution or data leakage, keeping the risk bounded within the Important classification.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A certificate validation flaw has been discovered in the golang crypto/x509 module. When verifying a certificate chain which contains a certificate containing multiple email address constraints which share common local portions but different domain portions, these constraints will not be properly applied, and only the last constraint will be considered.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Incorrect enforcement of email constraints in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because unauthenticated network entities can bypass identity restrictions without requiring local system privileges. In Red Hat environments hosting Go-based network services or container infrastructure, certificate chain validation overlooks specific email name constraints when multiple rules share an identical local mailbox name across distinct domain names. As a result, a subordinate certificate authority could successfully issue unauthorized certificates that circumvent organizational security policies, leading to improper trust establishment.

cwe.name: Incorrect Behavior Order: Authorization Before Parsing and Canonicalization

notes.text: A flaw was found in gRPC-Go, the Go language implementation of gRPC. This vulnerability, an authorization bypass, is caused by improper input validation of the HTTP/2 `:path` pseudo-header. A remote attacker can exploit this by sending raw HTTP/2 frames with a malformed `:path` that omits the mandatory leading slash. This allows the attacker to bypass defined security policies, potentially leading to unauthorized access to services or information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc/grpc-go: google.golang.org/grpc/authz: gRPC-Go: Authorization bypass due to improper HTTP/2 path validation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact for Red Hat because remote unauthenticated attackers could bypass access restrictions, potentially compromising service integrity and exposing sensitive internal data across affected endpoints. To successfully exploit this issue, services must implement path-based authorization interceptors that enforce specific deny rules while permitting other requests through a fallback allow configuration. Typical Red Hat product deployments configure components with strict default-deny policies or transport-level mutual TLS, restricting the practical attack surface to non-standard environments.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: To start using the DevWorkspace Operator, install the DevWorkspace Operator from OpenShift OperatorHub on OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 or higher.

To mitigate this issue, implement infrastructure-level normalization to ensure all incoming HTTP/2 `:path` headers are properly formatted with a leading slash before reaching the gRPC-Go server. This can be achieved by configuring a reverse proxy or API gateway to validate and normalize the `:path` header. Ensure that any such intermediary is properly configured and restarted to apply the changes, which may temporarily impact service availability.

which add new features and enhancements, bug fixes, and updated container images.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
The multicluster engine for Kubernetes v2.6 images

The multicluster engine for Kubernetes provides the foundational components
that are necessary for the centralized management of multiple
Kubernetes-based clusters across data centers, public clouds, and private
clouds.

You can use the engine to create new Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform
clusters or to bring existing Kubernetes-based clusters under management by
importing them. After the clusters are managed, you can use the APIs that
are provided by the engine to distribute configuration based on placement
policy.

cwe.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Object Prototype Attributes

notes.text: A flaw was found in Lodash. A prototype pollution vulnerability in the _.unset and _.omit functions allows an attacker able to control property paths to delete methods from global prototypes. By removing essential functionalities, this can result in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: lodash: prototype pollution in _.unset and _.omit functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This issue is only exploitable by applications using the _.unset and _.omit functions on an object and allowing user input to determine the path of the property to be removed. This issue only allows the deletion of properties but does not allow overwriting their behavior, limiting the impact to a denial of service. Due to this reason, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.

In Grafana, JavaScript code runs only in the browser, while the server side is all Golang. Therefore, the worst-case scenario is a loss of functionality in the client application inside the browser. To reflect this, the CVSS availability metric and the severity of the Grafana and the Grafana-PCP component have been updated to low and moderate, respectively.

The lodash dependency is bundled and used by the pcs-web-ui component of the PCS package. In Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.10, the pcs-web-ui component is no longer included in the PCS package. As a result, RHEL 8.10 does not ship the vulnerable lodash component within PCS and is therefore not-affected by this CVE.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details:
For multicluster engine for Kubernetes, see the following documentation for
details on how to install the images:

https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.11/html/clusters/cluster_mce_overview#mce-install-intro

To mitigate this issue, implement strict input validation before passing any property paths to the _.unset and _.omit functions to block attempts to access the prototype chain. Ensure that strings like __proto__, constructor and prototype are blocked, for example.

cwe.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/url package in the Go standard library. The package does not enforce a limit on the number of unique query parameters it parses. A Go application using the net/http.Request.ParseForm method will try to process all parameters provided in the request. A specially crafted HTTP request containing a massive number of query parameters will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory, eventually causing the application to crash or become unresponsive, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/url: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be able to send a specially crafted HTTP request to an application parsing URL-encoded forms with net/url, specifically a request containing a large number of unique query parameters. The request will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory and eventually result in a denial of service, with no impact to confidentiality or integrity. Due to this reason, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.

cwe.name: Excessive Platform Resource Consumption within a Loop

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted certificate during the error string construction process within the `HostnameError.Error()` function. This flaw, caused by unbounded string concatenation, leads to excessive resource consumption. Successful exploitation can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the affected system.

By manipulating specific APIs such as mergeDeep(), mergeDeepWith(), merge(), Map.toJS(), and Map.toObject(), a remote attacker could potentially execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (DoS).

In most deployments, the ability to provide data in this fashion requires that an attacker has some degree of privileges to access the affected applications.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Axios, a promise-based HTTP client. This vulnerability occurs because Axios does not correctly handle hostname normalization when evaluating NO_PROXY rules. An attacker can exploit this by crafting requests to loopback addresses (e.g., localhost. or [::1]) which bypass the NO_PROXY configuration and are routed through the configured proxy. This can lead to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities, enabling attackers to access sensitive internal or loopback services that should otherwise be protected.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: axios: Axios: Server-Side Request Forgery and proxy bypass due to improper hostname normalization
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This flaw has limited impact due to combination of non-default conditions to exploit: the attacker must be able to control or influence URLs passed to axios in a server-side context, the application must have both `HTTP_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` configured, and the proxy itself must be positioned to act on the misdirected traffic or have been compromised by the attacker to intercept the rerouted traffic.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Python-Markdown. Parsing crafted markdown content containing malformed HTML-like sequences causes html.parser.HTMLParser to raise an unhandled AssertionError. This unhandled exception allows an attacker to cause an application crash and potentially disclose sensitive information via its stack trace.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python-markdown: denial of service via malformed HTML-like sequences
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be able to supply a specially crafted payload to be processed by an application using Python-Markdown. Additionally, the security impact of this vulnerability is limited to an information disclosure via the unhandled exception stack trace and a denial of service. There is no memory corruption or arbitrary command execution. Due to these reasons, this issue has been rated with an important severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more about Red Hat Developer Hub, see References links
To mitigate this vulnerability, wrap your markdown parsing function in a try/except block. This catches the unhandled exception, preventing both the application crash and the stack trace leak.

notes.text: A flaw was found in ajv. When the $data option is enabled, the value of the pattern keyword is passed directly to the JavaScript RegExp() constructor without sufficient validation. An attacker able to supply a malicious regular expression pattern can trigger a ReDoS (Regular Expression Denial of Service), causing the application to become unresponsive and resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: ajv: ReDoS via $data reference
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this issue, the $data option must be enabled and the attacker needs to be able to send a payload with a specially crafted regular expression to the application processing the input. A 31-character payload causes approximately 44 seconds of execution, with each additional character doubling the execution time. Therefore, even a small payload can cause an application to become unresponsive and eventually result in a denial of service. Due to this reason, this flaw has been rated with an important severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

remediations.details: For more about Red Hat Developer Hub, see References links

To mitigate this issue, disable the $data feature if your application does not require it. If $data must be used, implement strict validation of the input fields that are referenced by the pattern keyword to ensure they contain only expected and safe characters.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici, a Node.js HTTP/1.1 client. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending HTTP/1.1 requests that include duplicate Content-Length headers with different casing (e.g., "Content-Length" and "content-length"). This can lead to HTTP Request Smuggling, a technique where an attacker sends an ambiguous request that is interpreted differently by a proxy and a backend server. Successful exploitation could result in unauthorized access, cache poisoning, or credential hijacking. It may also cause a Denial of Service (DoS) if strict HTTP parsers reject the malformed requests.

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact. A flaw in the undici Node.js HTTP/1.1 client allows for HTTP Request Smuggling or Denial of Service. This can occur in Red Hat products that use undici and process HTTP requests where user-controlled header names are not case-normalized, or headers are passed as flat arrays.

The Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security is not affected by this issue since it's shipping a `path-to-regexp` version which doesn't contain the vulnerable code.

notes.text: Red Hat evaluates this vulnerability as having an Important severity because unauthenticated remote attackers can target exposed Go services over the network to trigger severe denial-of-service conditions or validation discrepancies without requiring elevated privileges. notes.text: A flaw was found in Underscore.js, a JavaScript utility library. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) attack by providing specially crafted recursive data structures. When these structures are processed by the _.flatten or _.isEqual functions, which lack a depth limit for recursion, a stack overflow occurs. This can make the application unavailable to legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: Underscore.js: Underscore.js: Denial of Service via recursive data structures in flatten and isEqual functions
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

To mitigate this issue, applications utilizing Underscore.js should ensure that any processing of untrusted, recursively structured data with `_.flatten` or `_.isEqual` explicitly enforces a finite depth limit. Review application code to identify and modify calls to these functions, adding appropriate depth parameters to prevent stack overflow conditions. Additionally, input validation should be implemented to sanitize untrusted data before it is processed by Underscore.js functions.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Backstage. The backstage/plugin-techdocs-node package uses an allowlist to filter dangerous MkDocs configuration keys during the documentation build process. Additionally, an attacker can execute arbitrary Python code but the payload is confined by the permissions granted to the TechDocs build process which is typically a restricted service account, limiting the impact of this vulnerability. Due to these reasons, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Axios, a promise-based HTTP client. This vulnerability, known as Prototype Pollution, can be exploited through a specific "Gadget" attack chain. This allows an attacker to escalate a Prototype Pollution vulnerability in a third-party dependency, potentially leading to remote code execution or a full cloud compromise, such as bypassing AWS IMDSv2.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: axios: Axios: Remote Code Execution via Prototype Pollution escalation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
The Axios library, a promise-based HTTP client, is susceptible to an Important prototype pollution vulnerability. This flaw, when combined with specific "Gadget" attack chains in third-party dependencies, can lead to remote code execution or full cloud compromise, including bypassing AWS IMDSv2.
 
With pollution check patch available in Axios gives an advantage, it remains vulnerable due to HTTP Header Sanitation and Server-Side Request Forgery threat.

Red Hat products that incorporate the vulnerable Axios library are affected.

The openshift4/ose-monitoring-plugin-rhel9 container image is not vulnerable to this flaw. The affected component is used as a build-time dependency but it's not shipped in the final product, meaning the flaw is not present thus cannot be exploited in the container deployments.

Regarding openshift4/ose-console for Product stream 4.12 and 4.13, the vulnerable component is present (indirect dependency), but the vulnerability is not exploitable in our case due to the browser runtime, where the required Node.js-specific attack vectors are not available. With this, the impact becomes low.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/url package in the Go standard library. The package does not enforce a limit on the number of unique query parameters it parses. A Go application using the net/http.Request.ParseForm method will try to process all parameters provided in the request. A specially crafted HTTP request containing a massive number of query parameters will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory, eventually causing the application to crash or become unresponsive, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/url: Memory exhaustion in query parameter parsing in net/url
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: To exploit this flaw, an attacker must be able to send a specially crafted HTTP request to an application parsing URL-encoded forms with net/url, specifically a request containing a large number of unique query parameters. The request will cause the application to consume an excessive amount of memory and eventually result in a denial of service, with no impact to confidentiality or integrity. Due to this reason, this vulnerability has been rated with an important severity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

There is no mitigation for this issue other than updating the Go toolchain to Go 1.25.12 or Go 1.26.5. Programs compiled with Go >= 1.24 that do not use the os.Root API are not affected by this vulnerability.
The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected.

When these malformed email addresses are parsed by the `consumePhrase` function, it can lead to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic string concatenation, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/mail: golang: net/mail: Denial of Service via pathological email address parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `net/mail` package of the Go standard library. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by sending specially crafted email addresses, leading to excessive resource consumption and a denial of service in Go applications that parse email addresses using the affected library.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) package. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is rated as an Important severity flaw. A remote attacker could trigger a Denial of Service by sending a crafted MIME header with numerous invalid encoded-words to an application utilizing the affected Golang MIME package. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption on the system processing the malformed header, impacting service availability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.
notes.title: CVSS score applicability

system have been applied. For details on how to apply this update, refer to:

To mitigate this issue, restrict network access to services that process MIME headers from untrusted sources. Implement input validation and sanitization for all incoming data, especially MIME headers, to prevent maliciously crafted content from being processed by applications utilizing the vulnerable Golang MIME package.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.

Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost/compress package. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by supplying a specially crafted compression dictionary with an excessively large repeat value, triggering an integer overflow. When the dictionary is subsequently processed, this overflow leads to out-of-bounds memory access, crashing the application and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via integer overflow in dictionary processing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has rated this vulnerability as having an impact of Important because an unauthenticated remote attacker could trigger a denial of service by causing a process crash without requiring elevated permissions. In Red Hat environments where this Go library is embedded, exploitation requires that an application accepts untrusted dictionary structures for S2 compression and subsequently attempts encoding. Although the resulting memory access fault terminates the vulnerable process, the flaw is confined to process crashes and does not compromise data confidentiality or integrity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/net/idna. ToASCII and ToUnicode incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only hostname (for example, xn--example-.com returns example.com instead of an error). notes.text: golang.org/x/net/idna is vulnerable to privilege escalation through incorrect Punycode label handling in ToASCII and ToUnicode. Red Hat exposure is broad across products shipping the Go toolchain or bundling golang.org/x/net, including RHEL and RHEL-AI golang RPMs, hummingbird Go runtimes, OpenShift and ODF container builds, and Ceph/OpenShift components compiled against affected x/net versions.

cwe.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `os.Root` functionality of Go on Unix systems. This vulnerability allows an attacker to bypass intended directory restrictions by crafting a path that ends with a symbolic link and a trailing slash. When a file is opened in `os.Root` with such a path, the symbolic link is improperly followed, potentially leading to access to locations outside of the defined root directory. This could result in information disclosure or unauthorized file system access.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: Go os.Root: Symlink following vulnerability allows directory traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in Go's os.Root implementation. On Unix systems, `os.Root.Open()` improperly follows symlinks to locations outside the root directory when the path ends with a trailing slash (e.g., root.Open("symlink/")). This is because `openat()` with `O_NOFOLLOW` does not prevent symlink resolution when the path has a trailing /. An attacker able to create symlinks within an os.Root directory could use this to read or write files outside the intended root. The os.Root API was introduced in Go 1.24. Go versions prior to 1.24 are not affected. This issue is fixed in Go 1.25.12 and Go 1.26.5.

The following symbols are affected:
* `OpenInRoot`: Opens a file or directory within an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Create`: Creates a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.Open`: Opens a path relative to an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenFile`: Opens a file with specified flags and permissions inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.OpenRoot`: Opens a sub-root directory from an `os.Root`.
* `Root.ReadFile`: Reads a file inside an `os.Root`.
* `Root.WriteFile`: Writes a file inside an `os.Root`.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

As a result, excessive resource allocation remains constrained to the specific worker process or container parsing the file, mitigating wider system failure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in qs. The `qs.stringify` function, responsible for serializing objects, does not properly validate the `isBuffer` property of an object's constructor before attempting to invoke it. An unauthenticated attacker can provide specially crafted input that, when processed and then serialized by `qs.stringify`, triggers a `TypeError`. This vulnerability can lead to a Denial of Service (DoS), causing affected applications to return a 500 error or, in certain scenarios, terminate the application process.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: qs: qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

As a workaround until packages are updated, avoid using BalancedPool for any connection that relies on custom TLS certificate validation (e.g. certificate pinning); use Client, Pool, or Agent instead, which are unaffected. cwe.name: Origin Validation Error

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When the cache or deduplicate interceptor is directly composed onto a Client or Pool, the destination origin is omitted from cache and request-deduplication keys. This allows a remote attacker to perform cross-origin cache poisoning, leading to information disclosure and potentially a full authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit this by having a trusted origin accept a malicious token, without contacting the legitimate trusted origin.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Authentication bypass via cross-origin cache poisoning due to missing origin isolation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. A remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by initiating a Transport Layer Security (TLS) renegotiation and presenting a certificate with a mismatched hostname. Because the client application fails to properly handle the resulting verification error, an uncaught assertion is triggered, terminating the client process and disrupting active network requests.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via TLS renegotiation with mismatched certificate
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is evaluated as an Important severity flaw for Red Hat products because an unauthenticated remote server can terminate a client Node.js process, halting all concurrent tasks and in-flight operations. In typical Red Hat deployments, containerized microservices and administrative consoles rely on undici or runtime fetch APIs to communicate with external web endpoints. Exploitation requires the client application to establish an outbound TLS 1.2 connection to a malicious or compromised endpoint that initiates session renegotiation with a non-matching certificate. Workloads communicating strictly with trusted endpoints or utilizing TLS 1.3 connections are inherently protected, as TLS 1.3 does not permit server-driven renegotiation.

While this flaw allows service interruption without requiring privileges, it does not lead to code execution or compromise data confidentiality and integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. This vulnerability may allow a remote attacker to intercept or modify encrypted communications by bypassing custom certificate validation. The issue occurs because the Agent dispatcher discards caller-supplied Transport Layer Security (TLS) verification functions during internal configuration copying, causing the client to silently ignore application-specific checks such as certificate or public-key pinning.

notes.text: undici: undici: Certificate validation bypass via dropped TLS options in Agent
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having an Important severity for Red Hat products because an attacker positioned on the network could bypass custom cryptographic protections, allowing the interception or tampering of sensitive traffic. Standard system trust stores and default certificate chain validations are not compromised by this flaw, which reduces exposure for environments relying solely on standard public key infrastructure. The elevated risk is restricted to services and applications that configure specialized certificate validation handlers, such as explicit certificate or public key pinning, when establishing outbound connections.

cwe.name: Origin Validation Error

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When an application configures redirect handling alongside a shared cache, responses received after cross-origin redirects are incorrectly stored under the initial request URL. A remote attacker who controls a redirect destination can exploit this vulnerability to poison the shared cache, serving malicious content to subsequent users requesting trusted URLs. Additionally, this behavior can result in information disclosure if private or user-specific responses are cached and delivered to unauthorized callers.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Cache poisoning and information disclosure via improper cross-origin redirect caching
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important severity because successful exploitation enables remote attackers to achieve shared cache poisoning and unauthorized cross-user data exposure across network boundaries without requiring elevated privileges. Within Red Hat environments shipping Node.js runtimes and associated container services, undici is utilized as an HTTP client backend. However, exploitation requires a specific application architecture where an originless dispatcher chains redirect processing ahead of a shared cache store, rather than the default standalone client configurations. Deployments that do not implement shared caching across multi-origin redirect flows or that isolate cache storage per origin remain unaffected by this flaw.

cwe.name: Uncaught Exception

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. A malicious remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by returning an invalid handshake response when a client attempts to establish a WebSocket connection over HTTP/2. The client mishandles the failed connection setup and leaves the underlying network stream open without an error handler. When the remote server subsequently terminates the connection, an unhandled error is raised, causing the application process to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via failed HTTP/2 WebSocket handshake
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important impact because an unauthenticated remote endpoint can trigger an unhandled exception that terminates the entire Node.js application process, resulting in a complete denial of service. The risk primarily impacts client applications or services configured to open outbound WebSocket sessions over HTTP/2 to untrusted or external servers. In typical Red Hat environments, many bundled container services connect exclusively to controlled internal infrastructure, substantially reducing the likelihood of encountering an adversarial endpoint.

cwe.name: Uncaught Exception

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When an application sends a request to a malicious remote server, the server can return a response with excessive content encodings and immediately close the connection. Because the underlying response stream is left unhandled, this abrupt closure triggers an unhandled error that causes the application process to crash. Consequently, an attacker operating a remote server can cause a Denial of Service (DoS), terminating the application even if standard error handling is implemented.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Denial of Service via unhandled stream error on excessive content encodings
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity because an unauthenticated remote server can trigger an unhandled runtime error that abruptly terminates the parent Node.js process, bypassing application-level catch blocks. In Red Hat products and containerized workloads running affected Node.js runtimes, the flaw impacts services executing outbound HTTP calls to untrusted or external third-party endpoints. Conversely, deployments where applications only interact with verified internal endpoints or do not fetch content from untrusted remote hosts are not exposed to this denial-of-service condition.

cwe.name: Out-of-bounds Read

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a specially crafted Zstandard (zstd) compressed stream to an application using the library, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS). Due to an integer handling error in the decompression logic, the decoder retains stale internal state and performs an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled panic that crashes the application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: github.com/klauspost/compress/zstd: klauspost/compress: Denial of Service via crafted zstd compressed input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the klauspost compress library's Zstandard (zstd) decompression implementation. An integer handling flaw in the FSE normalized count parsing logic allows a remote attacker to supply a specially crafted two-block compressed stream. When processed by vulnerable decode routines, the parser retains stale decode-table state and executes an out-of-bounds read, triggering an unhandled runtime panic. Applications decompressing untrusted inputs will terminate abruptly, causing a denial of service, while container boundaries and non-root execution isolate the impact from the underlying host.
notes.title: Statement

For Cluster Observability Operator 1.5, see the following instructions to apply this update:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_cluster_observability_operator/1-latest

Reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. No direct configuration-level workaround exists within the library itself.

--- CME Mitigation Guidance (2026-11-03) ---
Disclaimer: The following mitigation solutions are provided as a courtesy, pending the application of an official patch. This content was generated utilizing AI tools in conjunction with data from https://cmetaxonomy.org. Customers are advised to independently evaluate and test these temporary mitigations within their own infrastructure.

The highest-value action is to enforce bounds on parsed count values and decode-table indices in klauspost/compress zstd decompression routines to prevent integer wraparound and out-of-bounds indexing: upgrade to klauspost/compress 1.20.2+ (or the corresponding fixed Red Hat builds), which reject counts exceeding math.MaxInt16 in readNCount, restrict Huffman-weight FSE tableLog values to 6 in huff0.ReadTable, and adjust count validation in validateNorm, closing crafted two-block zstd compressed stream. Until patched, this is a concern on applications decompressing untrusted Zstandard (zstd) input using klauspost/compress DecodeAll or streaming decoder, so reject or filter untrusted Zstandard-compressed payloads at ingress proxies, or restrict decompression endpoints to authenticated, trusted clients. These controls limit blast radius and contain exploitation, but they do not fix the underlying integer wraparound defect — apply the upstream patch to fully remediate.

Highest-impact CME: CME-1311 Input Size and Quantity Bounds Enforcement (high)

* golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)

* golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header (CVE-2026-42504)

* golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service (CVE-2026-56853)

* golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input (CVE-2026-56858)

* golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue (CVE-2026-56859)

* golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution (CVE-2026-56860)

* golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

remediations.details:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package within the Go (golang) standard library, specifically affecting TLS 1.3 connections. A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending multiple key update messages in a single record after the handshake. This can cause the connection to deadlock, leading to uncontrolled consumption of resources and ultimately a denial of service (DoS).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Go crypto/tls: Denial of Service via multiple TLS 1.3 key update messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: A flaw in the Go `crypto/tls` package allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service in applications using TLS 1.3. By sending multiple key update messages in a single record post-handshake, an attacker can trigger a connection deadlock, leading to uncontrolled resource consumption. This impacts Red Hat products utilizing the affected Go standard library for TLS 1.3 connections.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) package. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a maliciously-crafted MIME header containing many invalid encoded-words. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: mime: golang: Golang MIME: Denial of Service via maliciously-crafted MIME header
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is rated as an Important severity flaw. A remote attacker could trigger a Denial of Service by sending a crafted MIME header with numerous invalid encoded-words to an application utilizing the affected Golang MIME package. This could lead to excessive CPU consumption on the system processing the malformed header, impacting service availability.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `net/http` component of the Go standard library. When a server is configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2, it reads initial bytes from new connections to detect the HTTP/2 client preface. However, the `ReadHeaderTimeout` is not correctly applied during this process. This oversight could allow a remote attacker to maintain open connections indefinitely, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) by exhausting server resources.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: Go net/http: Unencrypted HTTP/2 connections vulnerable to Denial of Service
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Important: Unencrypted HTTP/2 servers are susceptible to a denial of service due to improper handling of ReadHeaderTimeout during the client preface reading phase. This can lead to resource exhaustion and service unavailability in affected Red Hat products configured to support unencrypted HTTP/2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `html/template` component of Go (golang). Pathological inputs could prematurely close an unescaped forward slash ('/'), allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary content. This could lead to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), where malicious scripts are executed in a user's browser, potentially compromising user data or actions.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: Go html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Go `html/template` package. Applications utilizing this package to render untrusted input are susceptible to arbitrary content injection due to a flaw in how pathological inputs are handled, potentially leading to client-side script execution.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/xml` package of Go. The `DecodeElement` function failed to correctly track recursion depth, which could lead to stack exhaustion. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted XML input, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the affected application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/xml: golang: Go: Denial of Service via XML decoding recursion depth issue
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important denial of service flaw affects applications utilizing the Go `encoding/xml` package. This vulnerability arises from an issue in XML decoding where a recursion depth counter fails to reset, potentially leading to stack exhaustion when processing malicious XML input.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in `net/url`, a component of `golang`. This vulnerability arises when resolving relative paths that contain numerous parent directory ('..') segments. A remote attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted path, leading to quadratic time complexity and excessive memory allocation. This can result in a Denial of Service (DoS) due to resource exhaustion.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/url: golang: golang net/url: Denial of Service from quadratic complexity in path resolution
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go `net/url` package. Applications built with Go that process untrusted URLs containing parent directory segments ('..') may be vulnerable to excessive resource consumption due to quadratic time complexity in path resolution. This can lead to a denial of service, impacting the availability of affected services.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/tls` package, part of `golang`. A malicious client can exploit this vulnerability by continuously sending KeyUpdate messages to a server. This forces the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/tls: golang: Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service vulnerability in the `golang` `crypto/tls` package. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw by continuously sending `KeyUpdate` messages during a TLS handshake, forcing the server to perform indefinite key derivation operations. This resource exhaustion can lead to a denial of service for applications and services in Red Hat products that use the affected `crypto/tls` library and are exposed to untrusted network clients.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. The certificate verification process fails to block trust in intermediate certificates associated with a compromised Certificate Authority (CA). A remote attacker presenting a certificate signed by these intermediate authorities can impersonate legitimate servers during secure connections. This flaw can enable an attacker to conduct a man-in-the-middle (MitM) attack to intercept or alter confidential communications.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: crypto/x509: Man-in-the-middle attacks via untrusted intermediate certificates
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.
notes.title: Topic

notes.text:
An update is now available for the Red Hat build of Cryostat 4 on RHEL 9.

Security Fix(es):

* dompurify: Cross-site scripting vulnerability allows code execution (CVE-2026-49978)
* immutable-js: Denial of Service due to mishandling of large index values in List operations (CVE-2026-59879)
* qs: Denial of Service via improper validation in stringify function (CVE-2026-82417)
* golang.org/x/image/tiff: Denial of Service via invalid TIFF image (CVE-2026-46604)
* golang.org/x/image/vp8l: Denial of Service via excessive memory allocation (CVE-2026-46603)
* github.com/apache/thrift: Denial of Service via unbounded recursion in Go transports (CVE-2026-83663)
* github.com/apache/thrift: Denial of Service via improper handling of compressed data (CVE-2026-94637)
* github.com/apache/thrift: Arbitrary code execution via heap-based buffer overflow during frame compression (CVE-2026-91135)
* golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write (CVE-2026-39834)
* Golang html/template: Cross-Site Scripting via pathological input (CVE-2026-56858)
* Golang crypto/tls: Denial of Service via indefinite KeyUpdate messages (CVE-2026-56862)
* Golang encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal (CVE-2026-33818)
* Golang net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames (CVE-2026-78669)
* go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs (CVE-2026-88031)
* google.golang.org/grpc: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests (CVE-2026-84445)
* brace-expansion: Denial of Service via stack exhaustion from crafted brace patterns (CVE-2026-102276)
* proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet (CVE-2026-90711)
* handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (Program.blockParams) (CVE-2026-106446)
* handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass (CVE-2026-106445)
* brace-expansion: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion in nested brace patterns (CVE-2026-102278)

For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.

cwe.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `encoding/asn1` package in Go. An attacker could provide a specially crafted, deeply-nested Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) structure, leading to excessive recursion during the `Unmarshal` operation. This could result in stack exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) condition.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: encoding/asn1: golang: Go encoding/asn1: Denial of Service via excessive recursion in Unmarshal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This is an Important denial of service flaw in the Go encoding/asn1 package, as it can be triggered remotely without authentication. An attacker can provide a malformed ASN.1 structure, causing excessive recursion during unmarshalling and leading to stack exhaustion, which can render the service unavailable.

notes.text: A flaw was found in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. When a remote attacker attempts to write data larger than 4GB in a single call on an SSH (Secure Shell) channel, an integer overflow occurs in the internal payload size calculation. This vulnerability causes the write loop to spin indefinitely, continuously sending empty packets without making progress. The primary consequence is a denial of service (DoS), as the affected system consumes resources and prevents legitimate data transfer.

notes.text: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: golang: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: Denial of Service due to integer overflow in SSH channel write
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as having a Moderate impact because triggering the condition requires transmitting an unchunked payload exceeding 4GB in a single operation across an SSH channel, which represents an atypical pattern in standard deployments. In typical Red Hat environments and containerized applications consuming this Go package, network communications and data transfers are handled in significantly smaller buffers, substantially limiting realistic exposure. In the event of exploitation, the blast radius is restricted to process hang and denial of service via an infinite loop, without compromising system confidentiality or data integrity.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the golang.org/x/image/tiff component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a denial of service (DoS) by providing a specially crafted, invalid TIFF image. When the TIFF decoder attempts to process an image with an out-of-bounds strip offset, it can panic, leading to the unavailability of the affected system.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang.org/x/image/tiff: golang.org/x/image/tiff: Denial of Service via invalid TIFF image
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the golang.org/x/image/tiff package. The TIFF decoder does not validate strip offsets read from a TIFF Image File Directory (IFD) before dereferencing them. Processing a specially crafted, invalid TIFF image with an out-of-bounds strip offset triggers a runtime panic, causing a denial of service in any application that decodes attacker-supplied TIFF images, such as thumbnail generators, document processors, or image upload handlers. Exploitation requires the application to decode a malicious TIFF file supplied by the attacker (CVSS UI:R); there is no impact to confidentiality or integrity, only availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. notes.text:

A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. A flaw was found in go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver for version < 1.17.10 and < 2.9.1. 
Improper handling of data query elements in the GridFS component can lead to a file identifier being misinterpreted as a query. An authenticated user can exploit this to delete all GridFS file chunks, making stored file content unreadable, resulting in a denial of service.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver: go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2: MongoDB Go Driver: Data deletion via query-operator injection in GridFS file IDs
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the MongoDB Go Driver. The GridFS component does not properly sanitize caller-supplied file identifiers before using them in database queries. A structured document passed as a file ID (for example, a BSON document containing query operators) is interpreted as a query condition rather than a literal match value. An authenticated attacker who can influence the file identifier passed to GridFS operations such as Delete, DownloadToStream, or OpenDownloadStream in an affected application can exploit this to delete all chunks in a GridFS bucket, resulting in permanent data loss and denial of service.
The practical impact depends on whether the product's code passes externally-controlled values as GridFS file identifiers.

notes.text: A flaw was found in proxy-addr. When an application defines trusted proxy subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses with an improper prefix length, the subnet parser fails open and erroneously treats all incoming network addresses as trusted. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by submitting a forged X-Forwarded-For header to spoof their client IP address. This flaw allows attackers to bypass IP-based access controls, rate limiting, and audit logging.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: proxy-addr: proxy-addr vulnerable to IP spoofing via IPv4-mapped IPv6 trust subnet
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as Important because unauthenticated remote attackers can spoof client IP addresses and circumvent security controls, such as rate limits or network access lists, by sending custom forwarding headers. Exploitation is contingent on application configurations that define reverse proxy trust subnets using IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation with short IPv4 prefix lengths. Environments configuring trusted proxies via canonical IPv4 CIDR blocks, hostnames, or default loopback addresses are not vulnerable to this behavior.

To mitigate this flaw through configuration:

1. Configure trusted proxy definitions using standard IPv4 notation (such as `10.0.0.0/8`) rather than IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation.
2. If IPv4-mapped IPv6 notation is required, set the subnet prefix length to at least 97 to cover the mapped boundary (for example, specify `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` instead of `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8`).
3. Alternatively, sanitize or strip incoming `X-Forwarded-For` headers at edge load balancers or boundary reverse proxies before passing traffic to backend applications.
